title: Purpose Document
description: A structured statement of what a buying agent is trying to achieve, written and cryptographically bound BEFORE the outcome is knowable, so that the outcome can later be graded against it. The document separates machine-checkable constraints from LLM-graded objectives.

schemaVersion.description: Semver of this schema. Verdicts are only comparable within a major version.

purposeId.description: Stable identifier. Phrasing variations and repeats all reference the same purposeId.

issuedAt.description: When the purpose was sealed. Must precede the first request.

issuer.description: Who is buying. Optional so purposes can be authored before an agent exists.

authoredBy.description: Provenance of the wording. Needed to detect whether one generator's voice is driving results.

summary.description: One line, plain language. This is the seed the phrasing generator varies. It is NOT the thing being graded.

inputs.description: Concrete referents the request is about: addresses, URLs, identifiers, date ranges. Free-form, but every value here is checkable against the response.

constraints.description: HARD BLOCK. Every field here is evaluated deterministically, with no LLM involved. A violation is a fact, not an opinion, and is not contestable.

responseSchemaRef.description: URI of a JSON Schema the response must validate against. The strongest available constraint; prefer it when the output shape is known.

requiredFields.description: JSON pointers or dotted paths that must be present and non-empty.

requiredSubstrings.description: Literal strings that must appear. Use for concrete referents from task.inputs, not for phrasing.

numericBounds.description: Range assertions on extracted values. The clearest form of a falsifiable expectation.

objective.description: SOFT BLOCK. Graded by an LLM judge against the response. Written before the outcome exists, which is what makes 'was this good' a well-posed question.

goal.description: What the buyer is trying to accomplish and why. Context the judge needs to distinguish a technically-correct-but-useless answer from a useful one.

successCriteria.description: Independently gradeable statements. Two minimum: a single criterion collapses to a vibe check.

statement.description: Must be answerable yes or no by someone holding only this document and the response.

necessary.description: If true, failing this criterion caps the verdict at partially_served regardless of the others.

disqualifiers.description: What would make this NOT served even if the success criteria appear met. Required, and deliberately so: it is far harder to write a vacuous disqualifier than a vacuous success criterion, so this field is the schema's main defence against self-serving purposes.

outOfScope.description: Things the buyer is explicitly not asking for, so the judge does not penalize their absence.

rubricRef.description: URI of the judging rubric applied.

blinding.description: What the judge must not see. Withheld to prevent halo effects and to keep questions like 'does price predict quality' answerable from this data.

binding.description: Cryptographic seal. purposeHash is computed over this document with binding removed entirely, canonicalized per RFC 8785 and hashed with SHA-256.
